D006_m001.question:
It started about a year ago, maybe a bit more. At first it was this surge of energy — I was sleeping three, four hours and still going. I’d get to the office at 4 a.m., fire off emails, start three new projects before the team even arrived. My mood flips on a dime: one minute I’m on top of the world, talking big expansion plans, the next I’m snapping at my staff over nothing. Any little noise — the AC clicking, a car horn outside — pulls my attention away mid-sentence.

Around eight months ago, things got…strange. I began hearing this male voice commenting on what I’m doing, sometimes criticizing me, sometimes just narrating. It’s there even when I’m alone. I’ve also become convinced something is wrong inside my chest, like my heart is rotting or wired incorrectly, even though my cardiologist says I’m fine.

There have been times, for a couple of weeks straight, when the voices and that conviction about my heart were there, but my mood wasn’t especially high or low.

In the last three months I’ve crashed. I avoid friends, barely talk to my wife and kids. I feel useless, and sometimes, out of nowhere, I get this urge to just step into traffic or off a balcony. It scares me, but it also feels like relief. Running the company has become almost impossible.
D006_m001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m002.question:
I’ve been driving long-haul most of my life, but for about a year now things have really gone off the rails.

Around ten months ago I started feeling unusually “up.” I’d be on the road for days and barely sleep, just buzzing with energy, talking nonstop on the CB, planning three new business ideas at once. I’d take extra routes, volunteer for more loads, start big projects at home, then drop them because I couldn’t stick with anything for more than a few minutes. My mind jumps all over the place.

About eight months ago, on top of that, I began feeling these crawling sensations on my skin, like someone’s brushing past me in the cab or tiny bugs marching up my arms, but there’s nothing there. Sometimes I feel like I’ve been “signal-marked” for some special mission—like I’ve got a unique power to guide people on the highways. I catch myself using words like “roadcode” or “skin-sparks” that make sense to me but other people look confused.

The last three months, the high flipped. I’ve stopped caring about the truck, the ball games, everything. I’ve thought a lot about ending it—where I’d park the rig, how I’d do it. I’m missing runs, my dispatcher’s on my back, and I know I’m not functioning like I used to.
D006_m002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m003.question:
It’s been about a year and a bit since things really started to go off. For the last 10 months or so, my mood has been all over the place. On some shifts I feel on top of the world, talking fast, buzzing, pacing the halls even when I’m off the clock. I can’t sit still, I’m constantly starting things—charting, then cleaning, then messaging friends—but I don’t finish any of it. Then I’ll suddenly snap, get irritated with coworkers or patients over nothing.

Around 8 months ago, I started noticing this strange smell, like something rotten or burning, even in sterile rooms. No one else smells it. Sometimes my speech gets… jumbled. I know what I want to say, but it comes out tangled and people just stare at me, like I’m not making sense.

For a couple of weeks, even when my mood felt kind of “neutral,” I was convinced one of the doctors on my unit was secretly in love with me—reading into every glance, every text. The last three months, though, I’ve mostly felt flat. I don’t care about being a “good nurse” anymore. I’ve had these sudden urges to just step into traffic after a night shift or jump from the parking garage—no plan, just an impulse that scares me.
D006_m003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m004.question:
It’s been a little over a year since things started getting…strange. About ten months ago I flipped into this nonstop “on” mode. I pace around my apartment, jump from rewriting the pitch deck to sketching three new product ideas to reorganizing my kitchen at 3 a.m. I can’t sit still. Every little sound grabs me—the fridge humming, a car horn outside, a Slack notification—my attention just snaps to it and I lose my train of thought.

Around eight months ago, I also started having these weird taste experiences. I’ll suddenly taste metal or chemicals, or this sickly sweet flavor, out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating. I’ve become convinced something is wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or poisoned—but every test comes back “normal.” When I talk about it, my thoughts kind of spin off; I start explaining the runway, then it turns into how the investors are linked to the taste in my mouth, then to something about my gut being rewired. It’s hard to stay on one track.

In the last three months, since the company’s basically collapsing, I’ve pulled away from everyone. I ignore friends, dodge my cofounder’s calls. Some days I just lie there thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I keep thinking I’d be better off dead, though I haven’t figured out how I’d do it. It’s wrecked my ability to work; I’m missing meetings, letting deals die, but I can’t make myself care enough to fix it.
D006_m004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D006_m011.question:

Around a year and a half ago, the weird smells started. I’ll be in the dry dock and swear I smell something rotten or burning, but no one else does. Sometimes at home I smell perfume or cologne that makes me think my wife’s seeing someone. I get stuck on that idea, checking her phone, asking where she’s been, even when I know it doesn’t add up.

My wife says I sit there making odd faces and barely answer her, just “yeah” or “fine,” like my words dry up. That can go on for weeks even when my mood isn’t high or low—just flat, but the smells and suspicions keep going.
D006_m043.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m044.question:
It’s been a little over two years since things really started to change. Around that time I began having these spells where I felt unusually “charged up” and on edge. For the past year and a half or so, I’m irritable most days—tiny things set me off, like the neighbor’s dog barking or the TV being slightly too loud. I pace a lot; I can’t seem to just sit and read like I used to. My daughter says I talk nonstop, jumping from one topic to another, and she can’t get a word in.

I’ve also had this embarrassing increase in sexual thoughts and urges that’s very unlike me, especially at my age and since my husband passed. It’s caused arguments with my family.

Alongside that, for about a year and a half I’ve noticed these odd smells—strong perfume or smoke—when no one else can smell anything. I sometimes catch myself doing little repetitive gestures, like tapping my fingers in a certain pattern before I sit or standing in a particular way, almost like a ritual. I used to be very active and organized as a nurse; now I struggle to initiate basic things—bathing, cooking, even calling friends—and some weeks those strange smells and beliefs linger even when my mood isn’t especially high.
D006_m044.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m045.question:
It started a little over two years ago, but in the last year and a half it’s really taken over my life. At work, I’m…overdoing it. I take on far too many projects at the library—reorganizing whole sections, planning new programs, staying late to “fix” things. I pace the stacks, can’t sit still at the desk, and my coworkers say I talk so fast they can’t follow what I’m saying or get a word in. My mood flips quickly: I’ll feel almost giddy and invincible setting up three new archives at once, then suddenly I’m snapping at people over something minor.

Around the same time, I started feeling these strange sensations, like someone brushing my arm or tapping my shoulder when no one is there. Sometimes it feels like something is crawling on my skin. It’s been going on for about a year and seven months. I’ve pulled back from friends and avoid social events at the library; people feel exhausting or suspicious.

For at least a couple of weeks at a time, even when my mood seems more “normal,” I still get those sensations and I’m convinced a man who visits the library is secretly in love with me, sending me hidden messages through how he returns his books.
D006_m045.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m046.question:
It started about a year and a bit ago. At first I just felt…amazing. Like I’d had ten coffees. On site I couldn’t stop moving—pacing, talking fast, jumping from one task to another. I barely sat down on breaks. I felt on top of the world for months, like nothing could touch me, like I was meant for something big.

Around the same time, I became convinced this woman from a TV show was sending me messages. Like, when she looked at the camera, that was for me, like we had this secret relationship. Even when I wasn’t feeling up or down, that belief stayed; it still feels real sometimes. I also keep smelling things that aren’t there—like burning wires or perfume—no one else smells it.

The last four months have been different. I’m slowed down, heavy. I move like I’m wading through mud, even climbing a ladder feels like too much. Stuff I used to enjoy—having beers with the guys after work, watching the game—does nothing for me now. I wake up a few times a night and then just lie there, going over every small mistake I’ve ever made, feeling like it’s all my fault and I deserve whatever bad comes my way. It’s gotten hard to keep working regular hours. Sometimes when I try to explain what’s going on in my head, my thoughts just fall apart and even I can’t follow what I’m saying.
D006_m046.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m047.question:
It started about a year and a bit ago. At first I just thought I was working hard, but it’s more than that. I’m a seamstress, I do wedding dresses, alterations. For the last 10–11 months I’ve been convinced my hands are… special. Like I’m chosen, that the dresses I sew can change people’s lives in some bigger way, almost like I’m famous and the whole town is watching me. I know it sounds strange, but it feels very real.

Sometimes, even when I’m alone in the workshop, I see people standing in the doorway, or figures sitting at the machines that aren’t there when I look again. Fabrics, faces, colors that don’t belong there. My words also get tangled: “thread, red, bed, dead” – I catch myself talking in rhymes instead of saying what I mean.

I’ve been on edge and snappy for about 10 months, starting too many projects at once, pacing, unable to sit, hands always moving. Then for the last four months or so, it’s like someone turned the pleasure off. I don’t enjoy sewing, TV, church, anything. I lie in bed for hours unable to fall asleep, going over little mistakes, feeling like my husband’s death was somehow my fault, that I should be punished. It’s gotten hard to keep up with orders or even open the shop some days.
D006_m047.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m048.question:
I’ve been working nights in the ER for a few years, and about a year and a half ago things started getting…different. For the last 11 months I’ve been convinced I’m meant for something bigger, like I have this special ability to “recode” people’s bodies just by being near them. Sometimes I hear what sounds like a male voice over the intercom or in my head, commenting on what I’m doing or telling me I’m “chosen,” even when the unit is quiet. I’ve caught myself using words like “bio-sparkle” or “shiftlines” and my coworkers look at me like I’m speaking another language. I know my face and tone don’t always match what I’m feeling; patients say I seem cold or flat.

For about 10 months I’ve been bouncing between feeling on top of the world—tons of energy, barely sitting still, flirting with patients’ family members, risky hookups after shifts—and then snapping irritably over nothing. I’ve called in sick multiple times because I can’t focus.

But the last 4 months, it’s like I crashed. I wake up at 3 or 4 a.m. and just lie there, replaying small mistakes from shifts years ago, feeling like I shouldn’t be a nurse at all. Moving and talking feel slow, like my words are stuck. I’m behind on charting, avoiding friends, and I can’t make myself care about anything, but I still feel guilty for everything that goes wrong at work.
D006_m048.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m049.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year and a half now. It really ramped up around last winter. I started getting convinced my ex-husband was sneaking around with people at his office, even after the divorce. I’d go through his LinkedIn, zoom in on pictures, read into every comment. Everyone tells me it’s over and none of it affects me anymore, but I can’t shake the idea he’s still lying to me somehow.

Around the same time I began seeing things—shadows of people standing in my hallway, faces in the corners of my vision. At work I sometimes see someone walk past my cubicle, but no one is there. My coworkers say I’ve become “flat,” but inside I feel like I’m either buzzing or collapsing.

For most of this time I’ve had these stretches where I’m “on fire”—talking nonstop, taking extra shifts, calling old clients, messaging people all night, pacing the apartment because I can’t sit still. Then it flips: for the last four months especially, I haven’t enjoyed anything. I lie in bed for hours unable to fall asleep, then pace or pick at my skin. I feel like everything that went wrong at work or with my daughter is my fault, like I deserve to be punished. It’s gotten hard to keep leading my team or even show up some days.
D006_m049.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D006_m050.question:
I’ve been on the road most of my life, but this past year and a bit, I just don’t feel like myself. About 11 months ago I started noticing weird things. Radio songs, billboards, even CB chatter feel like they’re aimed at me, like they’re commenting on what I’m doing or thinking. Sometimes when I’m driving, I suddenly get this strong taste in my mouth—like metal or chemicals—when I’m not eating or drinking anything. It makes me nervous to stop at certain diners or truck stops.  

Around the same time, I got… revved up. For about 10 months now I’ve been running on overdrive—hardly sitting still, pacing in motel rooms, taking extra routes just to keep moving. My mood gets way too high, like I’m on top of the world for no reason. My sex drive went through the roof; it’s caused real problems with my wife and my job.  

Then, about 4 months ago, things swung the other way. I started lying awake for hours before I can fall asleep, replaying every mistake I’ve ever made, feeling like I somehow caused accidents I just drove past. I keep pacing, picking at my hands, but I don’t even care about making my deliveries on time anymore. People say I sound flat, like I’m not really reacting to anything, and I can tell I trail off and start talking about other stuff mid-sentence. My work’s suffering, and things at home are hanging by a thread.
D006_m050.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
